4.a: (1) Reaction two needs the diatomic element balanced first — 4 goes before PCl3 and then 6 goes before Cl2 so the 12 chlorine atoms match, (2) Reaction one is direct — Na and Cl2 each appear once, so 2 before NaCl and 2 before Na finishes it, (3) Strategy — start with the element that appears in several compounds or inside a diatomic molecule instead of working rigidly left to right. A student who starts with P4 in reaction one or leaves Cl2 last in reaction two without checking the element inventory creates fractional coefficients or dead ends, revealing inability to strategize.

3.q: A local government authority denies a group of citizens permission to hold a peaceful, unarmed meeting to discuss civic issues, claiming it might cause inconvenience. Which category of Fundamental Rights is primarily being challenged here, and what limit would let the state restrict it?
3.a: (1) The challenged right — the Right to Freedom, specifically freedom of assembly under Article 19, (2) The permitted limit — only reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order may be imposed, (3) The verdict — a total or arbitrary denial of a peaceful, unarmed assembly infringes this guaranteed Fundamental Right, which citizens can enforce by approaching the Supreme Court or High Courts. A wrong answer reveals the misconception that the government has absolute control over public spaces and citizen gatherings without needing constitutional justification.
